description: Server sends CLOSE (half-closing its own write side), then keeps sending DATA anyway -- illegal per OVERVIEW.md section 2.5's receiving table, row 'half-closed (remote)': 'recv DATA -> RESET(STREAM_CLOSED)'. The RESET is fully autonomous: the client's own dispatch detects the violation and resets the stream on its own, with no scripted `send` step and no application action involved -- deliberately, so the assertion depends on the SDK's/adapter's own observation of the reset (a Stream's own recorded error for the Go/JS unit harnesses; the adapter's `stream_reset` event for the conformance runner), not on a runner-issued command or a wire-level fallback that would mask a suppressed event. Mutation-testing gap: a Go CloseWrite implementation that still lets a stray DATA reach the wire after CLOSE (mutation (b), see go/wsmixer/stream_test.go's TestStreamWriteAfterCloseWriteFails), or a client adapter that suppresses the resulting stream_reset event (mutation (d)), would both pass a fixture that only ever asserted stream_state:open -- this one exercises the actual half-closed(remote) violation end to end. No trailing `error_code: null` assertion here (unlike its siblings): the conformance runner's liveness probe for that assertion pings-and-expects-pong in --strict mode, which would collide with this stream's own already-in-flight, never-explicitly-consumed RESET frame sitting on the wire -- a real runner limitation for an autonomous stream-level RESET with no scripted `send` step, not a fixture compromise; stream_reset_code/stream_state already establish the connection stayed up (a connection-fatal error would leave no live stream to observe either field on).
